lesson.title: Chatbot, copilot, agent: what's the difference?
body: A chatbot answers when you ask. You type a question, it replies, and nothing happens until you ask again.

An agent is given a goal and works towards it in steps: it can open files, search, use apps and come back with a finished result. Microsoft's new Copilot Autopilot is described as an always-on agent you give a name, role and goal, which runs in the cloud and can be mentioned in Teams and Outlook.
More independence means more to check. An agent can act on your behalf, so be clear what it may touch, start it on low-risk tasks, and review its work before anything goes out.
lesson.takeaway: Chatbots answer; agents act. The more an AI tool can do on its own, the clearer your instructions and checks need to be.

m365.title: Get an email when a Power Automate flow fails
m365.what: Microsoft has been adding faster alerts for critical flows, apps and agents. You can already build your own: a 'Run after' setting makes an action run only when an earlier step fails, so you hear about problems straight away.
try: Open the flow in Power Automate and choose Edit.
Add a new action at the end, such as 'Send an email (V2)' from Office 365 Outlook, addressed to yourself, with the flow name in the subject.
Select the new action, open its Settings and find 'Run after'.
Tick 'has failed' and 'has timed out', untick 'is successful', then save.
Test it by making a step fail on purpose (e.g. a wrong file path), check the email arrives, then put the step back.

explainer.story: Energy bills set to jump in January
bullets: Ofgem confirms the 1 Jan–31 Mar 2027 price cap on Wed 25 Nov. Cornwall Insight's final forecast is about £2,166 a year for a typical dual fuel home, up £443 (26%) from today's £1,723.
The cause is high, volatile wholesale gas prices: the Middle East conflict has disrupted gas exports and European gas storage is at record lows going into winter.
Energy is already pushing up prices generally. UK inflation rose to 3.6% in October, and the Bank of England raised Bank Rate to 4% on 5 Nov.
explainer.why: It's the biggest single hit to household budgets this winter and will likely keep inflation, and possibly interest rates, higher for longer.

term.meaning: A fixed daily amount you pay for your gas or electricity supply, whatever you use. It covers costs like network upkeep and is capped by Ofgem alongside unit rates.
term.example: Ofgem has been asked to remove gas standing charges in 2027 or soon after, though timing isn't confirmed.

money.summary: Bank Rate is 4% and inflation 3.6%. Ofgem confirms January's energy price cap this Wednesday, with a rise of around 26% forecast.

money.tip: The price cap limits unit rates and standing charges, not your total bill. Taking a meter reading close to 1 January and submitting it to your supplier helps make sure usage before the change is billed at the old, lower rates.
